name.text: Relations Q8 - Restricting the domain of x squared

questiontext.text:
The function \(f(x) = x^2\), defined for all real numbers, does not have an inverse function because it is many-to-one. A teacher suggests restricting the domain to \(x \ge 0\). Why does this restriction allow the function to have an inverse?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

generalfeedback.text:
On all real numbers, \(f(x) = x^2\) is many-to-one, because a number and its negative have the same square. For example, \(f(3) = f(-3) = 9\).

An inverse function exists only when the original function is one-to-one, because the inverse must send each output back to exactly one input. For \(f(x) = x^2\) the output 9 would have to go back to both 3 and \(-3\).

Restricting the domain to \(x \ge 0\) removes the negative inputs. Different non-negative numbers have different squares, so every horizontal line now meets the graph at most once.

[[jsxgraph width="320px" height="240px"]] (function() { var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [-4, 9, 4, -1.2], axis: true, grid: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false}); b.create('functiongraph', [function(x) { return x*x; }, -3.2, 0], {strokeColor: '#9e9e9e', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 2}); b.create('functiongraph', [function(x) { return x*x; }, 0, 3.2], {strokeColor: '#1565c0', strokeWidth: 3}); b.create('line', [[-4, 4], [4, 4]], {strokeColor: '#c62828', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 2, fixed: true}); b.create('point', [2, 4], {name: '(2, 4)', size: 3, color: '#c62828', fixed: true, label: {offset: [8, 12]}}); b.create('text', [-3.6, 7.8, 'negative x removed'], {fontSize: 12, color: '#757575', fixed: true}); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

On the restricted domain the function is one-to-one, so its inverse \(f^{-1}(x) = \sqrt{x}\) exists. The correct answer is C.

Option A is wrong because the function still passes the vertical line test, before and after the restriction. Option B is wrong because removing inputs cannot create extra outputs, and many-to-many relations are not even functions. Option D is wrong because the restriction is exactly what removes the repeated outputs.

questionnote.text: Fixed: restricting x^2 to x >= 0, key C.

questiondescription.text: This question is based on the definitions of one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many relations in Section 16.1 (Types of Relations) of the Grade 11 Functions topic.

falsefeedback.text: Recall the condition for a function to have an inverse function: each output must come from only one input. Then ask what removing the negative inputs does to pairs such as \(3\) and \(-3\).
